reason: Verified in source and in the driven page. .b-rail (b.css 125) is a bare 1px fore-16 line from top:6px to bottom:0 with nothing declared at either end. Measured: rail top to the first tick is 287px at owner (px=18), 223px at desk/full (px=14), 191px at phone (px=12) - the finding's '282px' is right to the pixel-rounding. The terminus claim also holds: place() sets height = max(horizonDays*px + ROW(92), needed), so the rail runs 104px (owner) / 79px (desk, phone) past the wedding-day tick and stops in empty space. The 'today' anchor claim is understated rather than wrong: at 1440 the indigo .b-todayRule + 'Today is 16 July' sit 524px to the left across the gutter (not 400px) AND ~213px lower down the page than the rail's own top, so on desk and owner the two never line up and the measure column genuinely cannot be read on its own. The gates do not cover this (no assertion about rail termination or origin marking) and it is not a lessons.md repeat. The fix is in-palette and in-type, so no constraint is broken. It is only overstated on phone, where the indigo rule, 'Today is 16 July' and 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' all sit in the same column 73px above the rail and do state the origin in reading order - so the phone half of the argument should not drive the fix; the two-column states should.
sharpenedFix: Keep the intent, change three specifics. (1) Do NOT move .b-rail to top:0. top:6px is exactly the top edge a day-0 tick would occupy (.b-tick top:6px inside an item placed at away*px), so top:0 would start the line six pixels before today - the one thing this instrument must never do. Instead render the origin AT the day-0 tick line: a mark at top:6px, and give the rail an explicit terminus by ending it on the anchor tick (set the rail's height in place() from the last item's top + tick offset rather than leaving bottom:0), letting the 92px ROW tail below the tick stay unruled. (2) Do not put the origin label in the number gutter. Measured in the real 11px mono label style, 'Today, 16 July' is 117px and even 'TODAY 16 JUL' is 100px, against a gutter of 84px at >=1280 and 62px below it - it will overflow or wrap, and it would stack a second uppercase mono fore-62 label directly under the existing 'days away' head 22px above. Set the origin label to the RIGHT of the rail on the item lane (left:96px, matching .b-item), where the moment titles already start, so it reads as the first row of the measure rather than a second column header. (3) Scope it to the two-column states. On phone the horizon already delivers the indigo rule, 'Today is 16 July' and the gap sentence 73px above the rail; adding a second grey 'today' rule there duplicates the fact and competes with the one indigo moment on the surface. Apply the origin mark under [data-medium="sheet"|"full"|owner] only, and keep it fore-28 so the indigo horizon rule stays the only accented statement of today.
